description: `cleanUrls` array form with a Bash-style extglob pattern. Reference `serve-handler` honors extglob via `minimatch` at `serve-handler/src/index.js:59` — `+(page|other)` matches one or more occurrences of the alternation, so `/public/+(page|other).html` matches both `/public/page.html` and `/public/other.html`. The `sourceMatches` helper that runs minimatch is shared between `applicable` (cleanUrls, `index.js:265`) and `toTarget` (redirects/rewrites, `index.js:70`); the pinned reference's only dedicated extglob test exercises the redirects branch (`integration.test.js:449`), and the cleanUrls array test at `integration.test.js:705` uses a plain `/directory**` glob. This probe is the cleanUrls-side counterpart, capturing the structurally-implied extglob behavior on the cleanUrls path. Codex review round 3 P1 confirmed the divergence: irserve treats extglob constructs as literal characters (its `globset::GlobBuilder` does not support them), so the cleanUrls 301 does not fire. This probe captures the reference behavior and intentionally has no `runner.l0` block — it auto-skips against `target=irserve`. Tracked as Q-012 in `docs/reference/serve/open-questions.md` (closure options: implement extglob via regex translation; adopt an extglob-capable Rust crate when one materializes; or record an `adapted` D-NNN scoping IrServe to the standard glob set).
